Context: Horizonsmith runs a low-latency trading-decision service that scores candidate trades and re-ranks real-time signals. Primary goal is maintain p95 < 10ms across 2000-5000 QPS while keeping incremental inference cost under $0.003 per scored event. They operate across NA markets and require VPC deployment with strict key ownership (HSM preferred).

Customer quotes: 'We can't sacrifice tail latency for throughput' — lead infra. Also: 'If quantization saves 30% cost with <0.5% hit to buy/sell accuracy, we're interested.'

Technical requirements and preferences: prefer deterministic kernels, GPU pools with predictable throughput, automatic prefix/KV caching for repeated context, continuous batching up to 32 requests with 4ms max additional latency, option to route overflow to lower-cost quantized variant. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations: suggested batch sizes, cache TTLs for prefix hits, and quantization profile (4-bit QLoRA-style evaluation). Ask for perf benchmarks on their real trace (1M events) and a mixed read/write pattern that mimics market bursts.

POC success criteria: 1) p95 end-to-end < 10ms with 95% of requests served from dedicated pool; 2) cost per scored event <= $0.003 (including retries); 3) fallbacks in place to hosted quantized variant with <50ms degraded latency during capacity spikes.
